seo.title: Kaldewei Installation in Gerrards Cross | Fit-Only Steel Baths | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: We install client-supplied Kaldewei steel baths and shower trays across Gerrards Cross, protecting the enamel surface through the rest of the build. Fit-only, from £3,500.

hero.intro: A Kaldewei bath's enamel survives decades of daily use without a mark, but the vulnerable window is the renovation itself, when tilers, electricians and plumbers are still working around a bath that's already in place — and in Gerrards Cross, where we're coordinating a full strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging programme around 25 to 30 minutes from our Bracknell base, getting that sequencing right matters as much as the fit itself. We work fit-only across Gerrards Cross, the affluent Buckinghamshire commuter village close to Beaconsfield and Chalfont St Peter: you source the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture — including your Kaldewei bath or shower tray — and we handle everything from strip-out to snagging, from £3,500.

sections.heading: What we install from Kaldewei in Gerrards Cross
sections.body: Kaldewei's range runs from built-in, freestanding and bath-in-bath steel enamel baths through to low-profile and flush shower trays, matching panels and support frame kits, and combination bath-and-tray units. Kaldewei doesn't make brassware, so we fit whichever taps, fillers or shower valves have been specified separately, checking waste, overflow and tap-hole positions against the exact model first — a step we settle well before the strip-out and first fix begin, as part of the single coordinated visit a Gerrards Cross project usually needs.

sections.heading: Protecting a Kaldewei bath through the rest of the build
sections.body: Vitreous enamel on steel is extremely hard-wearing once a bathroom is finished and in daily use — it resists scratching, staining and heat far better than acrylic over the long term. During the build itself, though, it's vulnerable to a specific kind of damage: a dropped tile, a tool set down carelessly, or a sharp edge dragged across the surface can chip the enamel down to the steel base, and unlike a scratch in acrylic, that mark is permanent. On a Gerrards Cross project, where we're often coordinating a full strip-out, first fix, tiling and plumbing programme across a single, longer site presence rather than several short staged visits, we protect the bath or tray with board or heavy sheeting as soon as it's installed, and sequence the heaviest remaining trade work — tiling cuts, stone fabrication, any making good — to happen before the enamel surface goes in wherever the programme allows, rather than working around it afterwards.

sections.heading: Fit-only, strip-out to snagging
sections.body: We work fit-only across Gerrards Cross: you supply the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, including your Kaldewei bath or shower tray, and we carry out the strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging needed to install it, from £3,500, travelling out from our Bracknell base. A £125 survey comes first, where we confirm the installation sequence and plan how the enamel surface will be protected for the rest of the build. Book a survey to get a firm quote for your Gerrards Cross bathroom.

faqs.q: Does a Kaldewei bath need special protection during the rest of the build?
faqs.a: Yes. Vitreous enamel resists everyday wear once the bathroom is finished, but during the build a dropped tile or tool can chip it in a way that isn't repairable, unlike a scratch in acrylic. We cover the bath or tray with board or heavy sheeting as soon as it's fitted and sequence the remaining trade work around it.

faqs.q: How far is Gerrards Cross from your base?
faqs.a: Around 25 to 30 minutes by road from Bracknell. We travel out for surveys and installations across Gerrards Cross as a standard part of our coverage area.

faqs.q: Do you supply the Kaldewei bath, or do I?
faqs.a: You supply it. We're fit-only, so you source your Kaldewei bath, shower tray, brassware and tiles — and we strip out, first-fix, tile, plumb and snag it in, from £3,500.

faqs.q: What causes most damage to Kaldewei baths during a renovation?
faqs.a: Almost always it's later-stage trades — a dropped tile, a careless tool, debris from stone fabrication — chipping the enamel after the bath's already in place, not a fault in the product itself. Protecting the surface and sequencing the remaining work properly avoids it.
